title: High fever, diarrhea, confusion, poorly staining sputum in a smoker: Legionella pneumophila
vignette: A 63-year-old man is brought to the emergency department due to high fever, confusion, headache, watery diarrhea, and cough. The patient smokes 2 packs of cigarettes daily and has a history of chronic bronchitis. Temperature is 40.1 C (104.2 F), blood pressure is 100/70 mm Hg, pulse is 91/min, and respirations are 28/min. Sputum Gram staining reveals numerous neutrophils but no bacteria. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's current condition?

clues.text: high fever, confusion, headache, watery diarrhea, and cough
clues.note: Pneumonia with prominent GI (watery diarrhea) and neurologic (confusion, headache) symptoms plus high fever is classic for Legionella.

clues.text: smokes 2 packs of cigarettes daily and has a history of chronic bronchitis
clues.note: Smoking and chronic lung disease (plus age >50) are major risk factors for Legionella pneumonia.

clues.text: Sputum Gram staining reveals numerous neutrophils but no bacteria
clues.note: Neutrophils but NO visible organisms on Gram stain is characteristic - Legionella stains poorly with Gram stain (diagnosed by urine antigen/PCR).

whatMatters: High fever + GI symptoms (watery diarrhea) + confusion + a sputum Gram stain showing NEUTROPHILS but NO organisms, in an older smoker with chronic lung disease = LEGIONELLA PNEUMOPHILA. It stains poorly on Gram stain; diagnose with urine antigen or PCR. Answer C.
strategy: Combine the syndrome (pneumonia + diarrhea + confusion + high fever, sometimes hyponatremia and relative bradycardia) with the Gram-stain clue (neutrophils, no bacteria) and host (older smoker/chronic lung disease). Reject Coccidioides (Southwest fungal CAP, no diarrhea clue), Klebsiella (currant-jelly sputum, visible gram-negative rods), Mycobacterium kansasii (TB-like, chronic), and Mycoplasma (younger patients, milder 'walking pneumonia', high fever/confusion less typical).

eliminations.label: Coccidioides immitis - Southwest fungal CAP
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a dimorphic fungus endemic to the southwestern US deserts. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it can cause CAP but doesn't explain prominent watery diarrhea/confusion with a neutrophilic, organism-negative Gram stain; no endemic exposure given. ✅ Correct if: desert travel with pulmonary + erythema nodosum, spherules on histology.

eliminations.label: Klebsiella pneumoniae - visible gram-negative rods
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a gram-negative rod causing aspiration/nosocomial pneumonia (currant-jelly sputum). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it is readily seen on Gram stain and doesn't typically cause concurrent diarrhea; here no bacteria are seen. ✅ Correct if: alcoholic/aspiration with thick bloody sputum and gram-negative rods.

eliminations.label: Mycobacterium kansasii - chronic TB-like
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: an atypical mycobacterium causing TB-like illness. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it is subacute/chronic; high fever, watery diarrhea, and confusion are uncommon. ✅ Correct if: chronic cough/cavitary disease in COPD (acid-fast bacilli).

eliminations.label: Mycoplasma pneumoniae - younger, milder
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a common cause of 'walking pneumonia,' especially in younger patients. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: symptoms are usually subacute/mild; high fever with confusion and watery diarrhea point to Legionella. (Mycoplasma also lacks a cell wall and isn't seen on Gram stain, but the syndrome fits Legionella better.) ✅ Correct if: young patient with mild atypical pneumonia +/- cold agglutinins.

reasoning: Pneumonia with high fever, watery diarrhea, headache, and confusion is the classic Legionella syndrome
Sputum shows neutrophils but no organisms because Legionella stains poorly with Gram stain
Host factors (older age, heavy smoking, chronic lung disease) increase Legionella risk
mechanism: LEGIONELLA PNEUMOPHILA is a common cause of community-acquired pneumonia that classically presents with HIGH FEVER and fatigue followed by prominent GASTROINTESTINAL symptoms (watery diarrhea, nausea), pulmonary symptoms (cough, dyspnea), and NEUROLOGIC/constitutional symptoms (headache, CONFUSION); relative bradycardia and HYPONATREMIA are supporting clues. Patients over 50 who SMOKE or have CHRONIC LUNG DISEASE (or are immunosuppressed) are at greatest risk; outbreaks occur when the organism contaminates man-made water systems (hot tubs, cooling towers, plumbing). L pneumophila is a facultative intracellular, gram-negative organism that STAINS POORLY with Gram stain (its outer-membrane lipopolysaccharide takes up the stain weakly), so sputum shows abundant NEUTROPHILS but FEW/NO visible bacteria. It requires special media (buffered charcoal yeast extract with iron and cysteine); diagnosis is usually by URINE ANTIGEN test or PCR. Treatment is a respiratory FLUOROQUINOLONE or a newer MACROLIDE. The distractors are a fungal CAP (Coccidioides), a visible gram-negative rod (Klebsiella), a chronic mycobacterium (M kansasii), and a milder atypical pneumonia (Mycoplasma).

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Micro > Legionella pneumophila: high fever, diarrhea, confusion, hyponatremia, relative bradycardia; smokers/older/chronic lung disease; water sources; stains poorly (neutrophils, no organisms); buffered charcoal yeast extract; urine antigen/PCR; treat fluoroquinolone/macrolide.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Pneumonia + diarrhea + confusion + neutrophils without organisms on Gram stain = Legionella.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on Legionella, atypical pneumonia, urine antigen test, buffered charcoal yeast extract, or hyponatremia clue? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Coccidioides = desert fungus; Klebsiella = visible gram-negative rods/currant-jelly; M kansasii = chronic TB-like; Mycoplasma = younger/milder.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: Legionella = high fever + diarrhea + confusion + hyponatremia; poorly Gram-staining; urine antigen; smokers.

keywords.back: Age >50, smoking, chronic lung disease, water exposure

firstAid.detail: Micro: high fever, diarrhea, confusion; poorly Gram-staining; urine antigen.
Micro > Klebsiella, Mycoplasma, Coccidioides, M kansasii distinctions.

memoryHook: Legion of symptoms - lungs, loose stools, and a foggy brain, with a Gram stain full of neutrophils but no bugs (it won't take the stain): that's Legionella.
